Authorities arrested Stancil after he was found sleeping on a Florida beach on Tuesday. Bates maintains the confusion was inevitable, stating, "Believe me, it can happen to anyone," while the Oklahoma NAACP and state investigators are scrutinishing the Tulsa County Sheriff's Office's training records and treatment of minorities following the incident.

Mohamud, suspected as the "mastermind" behind the attack, is now believed to be across the border with Somalia leading Al-Shabaab militants. Pope Francis commemorated the 100th anniversary of the Armenian genocide by referencing his predecessor Pope John Paul II's 2001 declaration, reaffining the Vatican's commitment to historical continuity and moral consistency. The act, performed during a special Mass in Rome, underscored the church's sensitivity to diplomatic tensions and the perceived "unforgivable" nature of policy inconsistency.

The 30-year-old running back was suspended in November after he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor reckless assault following an incident in which he disciplarded his 4-year-old son with a "switch." Peterson, who is eligible for reinstatement after a district court judge vacated his suspension in February, is expected to join the Vikings for voluntary offseason workouts beginning Monday.

In February, a Minnesota district court judge vacated the decision that upheld his suspension, making Peterson eligible for reinstatement.

A Tulsa County reserve deputy mistakenly shot and killed a suspect during an arrest at a Dollar General parking lot, after the deputy believed he was deploying a Taser instead of his service weapon. The incident occurred as deputies attempted to arrest Eric Harris, who had fled and resisted arrest, and the 73-year-old deputy Robert Bates was placed on administrative leave as the investigation continues.

Chinese police arrested over 133,000 people and seized 43.3 tons of narcotics during a six-month anti-drug campaign. The operation also resulted in 115,000 drug-related crimes and 606,000 cases of drug use, though it came at a cost, with nine officers dead and 657 wounded. Authorities crack down on the industry intensified following a series of high-profile celebrity arrests.

Jack White announced a hiatus from touring to focus on an exclusive acoustic quartet. The tour will be limited to just five remaining U.S. states, with shows priced at $3 and sold on a first-come basis. Fans are scouring the Internet for his full touring history as the announcement's specifics remain vague.

CNN reports that UNICEF has been granted rare access to Sanaa Airport to deliver vital aid amid the ongoing conflict. With the airport previously bombed and hostilities likely to resume, a small window allows for the urgent distribution of emergency supplies to those in need. Despite the precarious ceasefire, the mission aims to ease the worsening humanitarian crisis affecting millions before any further evacuation or distribution.

Tomasz Lazar's photography project captures the haunting portraits of Polish survivors who were deported to Siberia as children during World War II. The images serve as a poignant reminder of a stolen generation, highlighting the emotional resilience and urgency to document their stories before it's too late.

Robert Bates, an Oklahoma reserve deputy charged with second-degree manslaughter in the death of Eric Harris, has released training documents his lawyer claims verify his qualifications. The records show Bates completed one Taser training class and qualified with a handgun 10 times between 2009 and 2014, though the family of the victim's attorney argues he was unqualified due to preferential treatment. A naturalized U.S. citizen from Columbus was arraigned Friday on federal charges of providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI. Abdirahman Sheik Mohamud, 23, allegedly traveled to Syria in 2014 for training and wanted to return home to kill Americans, particularly U.S. soldiers. Mohamud was remanded into custody and told someone he planned to attack a military facility or prison.

Airline pilots generally have above-average problem-solving skills, viewing the cockpit as a "safe place" structured by rigid procedures. However, the case of Andreas Lubitz highlights that untreated psychiatric issues can remain hidden; despite new FAA allowances for certain prescribed medications, his history of receiving injections for severe mental illness suggests that red flags were missed during the rigorous Germanwings selection process.

This week's pop culture highlights include the release of a new "Star Wars" trailer featuring Harrison Ford and Chewbacca, a viral logic puzzle about "Cheryl's" birthday, and ESPN reporter Britt McHenry's on-air car-towing incident. Additionally, Gisele Bündchen's retirement and a new book exploring online shame round the trends.

Warner Bros. and director Michelle MacLaren have parted ways over "creative differences" just weeks before the "Wonder Woman" film was slated to begin production. The studio confirmed MacLaren's departure on Tuesday, though the movie, starring Gal Gadot, remains scheduled for a June 2017 release. Warner Bros. will now search for a new director to helm the first theatrical film centering on the popular female superhero.

Hernandez confessed to the crime decades ago, but his defense argues he lacks the mental capacity to understand his actions, while a judge previously ruled his confession admissible. The case has long haunted the Patz family and the public, especially given the unresolved remains and the shadow of another suspect, Jose Antonio Ramos.

The project could go straight to series if it goes well, with Bob Kushell co-writing and serving as showrunner. The presentation is set to film next weekend on the Disney lot in Burbank with some of the original Muppet performers returning. Canadian actor Jonathan Crombie, best known for playing Gilbert Blythe in the "Anne of Green Gables" TV movies, died at age 48 from a brain hemorrhage. His co-star Megan Follows and producer Kevin Sullivan paid tributes to his "amazing chemistry" and dedication to the role. The "Anne of Green Gables" adaptation became a cultural touchstone, sp spining a fan following that extended to Japan and turned Prince Edward Island into a tourist destination.

Al-Shabaab's latest attack on Garissa University College, which left 147 dead, marks the deadliest assault in Kenya in over a year and a half. The group, steadily losing ground in Somalia because of African Union forces and U.S. drone moves, is targeting soft so-called targets like universities and malls rather than military bases.

In addition to that ruling, Judge Ronald Coen also lowered Knight's bail to $10 million from $25 million, a figure that defense lawyers called excessive. National Park Week, running from April 18 to 26, offers free admission to the 128 fee-paying U.S. national parks, including Yosemite and Yellowstone. The event, hosted by the National Park Service and Foundation, features activities like astronomy parties and Junior Ranger programs. Participants can explore sites via FindYourPark.com and share their experiences using the hashtag #FindYourPark.

CNN reports on the affordable housing crisis in Silicon Valley, highlighting families like Nicole paying $1,000 monthly rent for a one-car garage, while the broader issue affects 7.7 million low-income households nationally who spend over half their income on rent. HUD is launching preservation efforts and the Rental Assistance Demonstration initiative to protect existing affordable housing and combat the nation-wide crisis.

An American citizen was shot multiple times while driving in Karachi, Pakistan, on Thursday. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old California native, was struck in the right cheek and left arm but is expected to survive. Police believe the attack was motivated by anti-American pamphlets found in her car, and the U.S. Consulate General is working with Pakistani authorities to obtain more information.

A jury of Rolling Stone's media peers has determined that the magazine's discredited rape story amounted to journalistic malpractice, driven by the publication's refusal to hold the story after a Columbia University investigation found basic reporting lapses. The debacle stems from Sabrina Erdely's failure to verify attacker identity or give the fraternity a fair chance to respond, as she pressed ahead despite Jackie's increasingly inconsistent account.

Jon Cryer reprised his iconic record-store dance from "Pretty on the Outside" on "The Late Late Show," dancing alongside James Corden, who called it a "fulfilled childhood dream." The recreation celebrated the 1986 John Hughes film classic, reuniting fans who have aged alongside the movie's enduring appeal.

CNN reports that public outrage over "religious freedom" bills in Arkansas and Indiana caught governors "completely off-guard," despite knowing most Americans oppose such laws. Businesses, from the National Collegiate Athletic Association to Marriott International, have threatened boycotts, forcing politicians to "better adjust to a new reality." A 2014 poll found that 72% of millennials support same-sex marriage, signaling a shifting landscape for pro-business interests.

Ines Dumig's photo series "Apart Together" documents Sahra, a Somali refugee who fled her home at age 14 to seek asylum in Germany. The project explores Sahra's resilience and the universal themes of isolation and the search for human dignity. Dumig was drawn to Sahra's strength and ability to reflect on her experiences, aiming to universalize her story beyond just Sahra's individual narrative.

Jarret Stoll of the L.A. Kings was arrested Friday at a Las Vegas resort pool on a drug-possession charge involving cocaine and ecstasy. He was released on $5,000 bail, and the Kings organization has launched an internal investigation while withholding further comment. Stoll, a center with the Kings since 2008, was not with the team this season as they missed the playoffs.

Police in Marana, Arizona, initially believed a shoplifting suspect's gun was locked and inoperable, but the suspect, Mario Valencia, fired a shot into the air just 10 seconds after the employee reported it. A police officer then struck Valencia with his patrol car, ending the pursuit. Valencia was hospitalized and jailed on 15 charges related to the incident.

Two Delaware boys are in a coma and their father is unable to move two weeks after they fell ill, possibly from pesticide exposure, during a trip to the U Virgin Islands. The family was airlifted to hospitals in the United States, where the boys, aged 16 and 14, were in critical condition. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said Friday that the presence of a pesticide at the rented villa may have caused the illnesses. Exposure to methyl bromide can result in serious health effects, including central nervous system and respiratory system damage.

A suicide car bomb attack near the U.S. Consulate in Irbil, Iraq, claimed by ISIS resulted in at least four deaths and 18 injuries. All U.S. Consulate personnel were safe, and the State Department thanked the Kurdish government for its response while promising to investigate the bombing together. The United States pledged to continue standing with the people of the Iraqi Kurdistan Region as they work to confront these terrorist acts and towards defeating ISIS.

Over 300 suspects have been arrested in South Africa following deadly attacks on foreigners that killed two immigrants and three locals, including a 14-year-old boy. The government condemned the violence while praising police for preventing further bloodshed, noting the xenophobic sentiment is not representative of all citizens.

Davion Navar Henry Only, who spent his entire childhood in foster care, finally found a forever family after a viral plea for adoption led a minister's wife in Ohio to welcome him into her home. After years of hoping and waiting, his adoption was finalized on April 22, 2024, and with his new mother declaring, "I guess I always thought of you as my mom."

Democrats are increasingly focusing on economic inequality as they prepare for the 2016 campaign, but New Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer is po po likely to replace Harry Reid, a shift that alarms progressive advocates due to his Wall Street ties. Senator Elizabeth Warren is doubling down on her calls to break up banks, while Hillary Clinton and Martin O'Malley are also weighing in the debate over how to address wealth disparity.

Saudi Arabia has been bombing Yemen for three weeks to prevent Houthi rebels from consolidering regional dominance, with the U.N. Security Council voting for an arms embargo on the group. The conflict has killed over 648 civilians and wounded over 2,191, while increasing fears that Iran and Saudi Arabia are fighting a proxy war in the Middle East.

Joy Womack, a former Bolshoi Ballet Academy student, has been dancing with the Kremlin Ballet Theatre since leaving the Bolshoi in 2013 under disputed payment conditions. Now a principal ballerina performing near the Russian president's office, Womack earns roughly $240 a month (about $8 a day) as her salary has been devalued by the weakening ruble and sanctions; she relies on a friend for housing and takes extra engagements abroad to make her $185 bank account stretch for weeks.

Six Minnesota men, aged 19 to 21, were arrested for conspiring to join ISIS. The group, which included a significant Somali immigrant community, recruited one another through peer-to-peer methods. Four appeared in court on Monday, ordered to remain without bail as investigators seek to dismantle a network targeting young recruits.

Dr. Sanjay Gupta explores the evolving landscape of medical marijuana in "Weed 3: The Marijuana Revolution," addressing its potential benefits for conditions like epilepsy, PTSD, and multiple sclerosis while acknowledging the historical misinformation and long-term concerns regarding brain development. He highlights how it could serve as an alternative to painkillers given the overdose risks, and notes the federal study on its PTSD benefits. Overall, the piece serves as a comprehensive look into the science, the stigma, and the shifting perceptions surrounding cannabis therapeutics.

The study's authors say this public and easy attack will likely anger the international community, and China may have counted on that.

A German official said the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has not found a clear reason for the co-pilot's actions. However, the official said the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had suicidal thoughts before he became a pilot. Investigators have not found any letters or conversations where he explained his motives. Medical records also show that Lubitz was suicidal and received therapy before he got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group will not stop fighting. He stated that his fighters will not leave the main cities or the government institutions. He added that anyone hoping the group will surrender is mistaken.

His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition airstrikes aimed at pushing back the Houthis, who surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

Twenty years ago, on April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a truck filled with explosives into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The bomb killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and hurt many others. This event is the worst act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history.

The bombing shocked the nation. It was not just the size of the tragedy that people noticed, but the fact that Americans were attacking their own government in a way that had never been seen before.

If you care deeply about something, would you protest? Make a sign? Join a demonstration? How long could you keep going for, in the face of indifference and inaction?

When more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants, millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to plead for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people -- from celebrities to world leaders -- voicing their anger via #BringBackOurGirls, one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded.

CNN reports that Barney Frank, a retired congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He entertained a sold-out crowd at the Center on Halsted while discussing his 45-year career in public service. Frank made history as the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. He also had strong words for closeted politicians who vote against LGBT rights. When an audience member asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, Frank said he was not aware of the measure but told the young man not to worry about "c crazy people."

A brutal attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has left nearly 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while morning prayers were underway, shooting indiscriminately and taking hostages before being killed by security forces, officials said. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab militants have claimed responsibility. The harrowing attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab militants murdered non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been behind numerous attacks in the region. It has also recruited some Americans, particularly from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is taking down a statue of a British colonialist after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the removal of Cecil Rhodes' statue, saying his legacy is tainted with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, students started a campaign last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. The university announced Wednesday that the heritage authority granted permission to remove the statue from the campus. "These steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved," the university said in a statement.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An opposition group says the number of people who have died there has doubled in the last year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. A year before that, the death count was 162,402. The United Nations says the number was 70,000 the year before that. The United Nations also says that violence has pushed more than half of all Syrians into extreme poverty. They are in desperate need of help to survive because food rations have been cut due to a lack of donations.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was not silent or shy when it came to threatening a rival. According to a criminal complaint, she called a woman and said, "Leave my man alone." She also threatened, "Stop looking for him. ... I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Prosecutors did not consider this a joke and charged her with aggravated harassment, a crime she denies. Tsarnaeva is the sister of the men accused in the Boston bombings, Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

CNN reports that a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. The owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold the door for only $175 because he did not know it was valuable. The door is kept by the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza until a court date. Darduna’s home was destroyed last year, leaving him with only a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days into the air offensive, the coalition has destroyed the rebels' air defenses and disabled most of their airfields. Saudi naval forces now block all Yemeni ports, permitting only closely watched non-military medical supplies to enter. Locals are fleeing the violence, and the death toll is mounting, including many area residents.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry after his own fans booed Spain player Andres Iniesta. Hiddink called the fans a "disgrace." Spain lost 2-0 to Holland, but the Dutch fans booed Iniesta while he was warming up on the bench. Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored for Holland.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their Euro 2016 qualifier with Georgia will be played without fans in the stands. UEFA has started a disciplinary case against the Georgian Football Federation because fans twice invaded the pitch during Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Germany in Tbilisi. UEFA is also looking at charges that say home fans set off fireworks, and safety breaches like blocked stairs, locked gates, and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan invaded the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 defeat by Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

Football agents were left waiting on Wednesday after new rules were announced. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 to renew the licence every year. Existing agents were exempt from these changes. The FA was supposed to put a link on their website for agents to register, but as of 1pm it was still not there. Mel Stein thinks the new rules will 'create anarchy'. The new guidelines came in after FIFA washed their hands of governing agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not been paid for three months. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent.

Despite this financial problem, Uvarenko, who joined the Bulgarian club on an 18-month contract in January, is impressed by the fans and their passionate support.

"I still haven't received any salary and I've been at the club for three months," Uvarenko told local media.

David Moore, 25, got angry on the road after leaving his home and immediately got stuck in heavy traffic with Rafal Cegielka, 45. Cegielka was picking up his child from school. Moore then punched Cegielka and smashed his car with a hockey stick while children watched, all because he was having a "bad day."

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This game brought back bad memories of their poor performance at the 2014 World Cup. However, coach Vicente del Bosque is not worried about a third straight friendly defeat, says Gerard Pique.

Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the group stage last year in Brazil. That game marked the end of Spain's six-year domination of the world game. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena. They held on against some determined Spain pressure in the second half for a 2-0 success.

A New York City mother and named Ulrike Berger has fled to Germany with her daughter during a custody battle, police claim. Ulrike Berger, 44, is barred by a court order from leaving the country with seven-year-old Kaia. But on March 22, a day after the little girl was dropped off for a weekend visit, they are believed to have boarded a plane to Europe. Manhunt: Police are searching for Ulrike Berger, 44, (left) and her seven-year-old daughter Kaia (right). It is believed the pair boarded a plane from New York to Germany on March 22, violating a custody court order . Police say the pair were last seen at Berger's home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 1

Strong winds and dry weather caused a massive wildfire near the south coast. The fire started deliberately and burned through 70 hectares of heeland—an area roughly the size of 100 football playing fields. The fire came after several days of heavy rain and strong storms that had knocked down trees and shut roads. Investigators confirmed the fire was started on purpose in three separate spots.

Last night, emergency services were overwhelmed with 600 calls every hour as people across Britain celebrated the New Year. Ambulance services were stretched to the limit. In Cambridge, a military field hospital was set up to treat drunk partogers. At the peak, the London Ambulance Service was handling over 600 calls per hour—more than three times the normal amount. In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance while two revellers walked past eating a late night takeaway. Another man was slumped over in a doorway as two women celebrated the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him recover after he was dropped in December. Mignolet was dropped 'indefinitely' by manager Brendan Rodgers in December after a poor run of form but quickly returned after Brad Jones sustained a thigh injury. And the 27-year-old Belgian told how he tried to remain upbeat despite the disappointment at being axed. Simon Mignolet has revealed how his mental strength helped him recover after being dropped . Mignolet (second right) makes a save from a free kick during a league match against Swansea last month . Mignolet told FourFourTwo: 'I was positive.

Giant hailstones the size of plums crashed down over the South on Tuesday with residents rushing out to capture the freak weather. Twitter user Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls peppering his backyard and noisily plopping into the swimming pool. Footage shows the hailstones coming down at speed, with many cracking as they hit the ground. Despite it being around 80-degrees, the compacted lumps prove resilient to the heat taking a good while to melt. In a matter of seconds the patio is completely covered in snow-white pellets.

A replica pirate ship ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine. The ship, called the Liana's Ransom, lost power in rough seas and had to stop. The Coast Guard rescued nine crew members after they had to jump from the ship. The ship was left adrift in the ocean.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, the south coast of NSW, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'beautiful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A teenage boy named Rahul Kumar, 17, climbed into the lions' enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad. He was drunk. He began running towards the animals and shouted that he would kill them. Zoo security rescued him.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father said the boy was likely sleepwalking when he fell. The incident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi province in southeastern China. A woman working at a hotel across the road said she heard a loud bang around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a deep cut that almost cost him his eyesight. Miller says he feels very blessed the skate didn't hit his eye. He was very lucky. He skated with a full face mask during practice. He had a bad cut across his face that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. He has a scar across his eye, but doctors say he did not damage his eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to sign him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal last July but has struggled to get into the left-back position at Stamford Bridge. Atletico hope this might give them leverage, but Luis said: ‘I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.’

A Reading fan named Charlie Sumner got a three-year ban from football. He ran onto the pitch without a shirt and did somersaults during his first game at the Madejski Stadium last month. Sumner, who was 20 years old, did four front flips while the Royals beat Bradford City 3-0. He landed on his back and was stopped by stewards. Sumner said going to his first game was a 'brilliant experience'.

A video shows a group of men riding on top of a van as it swerved around a corner and flipped over. The incident happened on a road near the coastal city of Salé, Morocco. The van was carrying football fans when it started weaving from side to side on a busy road. The vehicle toppled on to one side at high speed.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions after winning last year's final in Malta on penalties against Holland.

To advance to the quarter-finals, England will have to overcome the Dutch again.

This tournament has been expanded from eight to 16 nations for the first time.

An annoyed elephant tried to spray a bull with water because the animal got too close. The elephant was relaxing in South Africa with its family near a small pool when the bull approached. In a photo, the elephant tried to squurt the bull with water from its trunk, but missed. The frustrated elephant tried again to spray the bull, which had wandered too close. Its young calf c huddled close to its parent for protection, while the bull drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe was convicted in 2006 for showing a Premier League game at his pub, the Stoke Inn. He spent eight years fighting to clear his name. Last week, a court overturned his conviction. Thorple says he lost his pub and paid a heavy price for the legal battle, but his name is now cleared.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at their home in Belfast might stop the June game against Romania. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and engineers checked it. The IFA said they noticed the damage on Tuesday morning. Northern Ireland's Windsor Park had overnight damage to its West Stand on Monday night.

A 20-year-old football fan ran onto the pitch at Reading's Madejski Stadium during a game against Bradford City. He took off his shirt and did four front flips before being stopped by stewards. He has been banned for three years because of the incident.

A BMW driver with five children was arrested after a student was killed while walking to the library. Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London. She was just weeks before her 22nd birthday. Friends left flowers at the scene and said she was 'much-loved and the most charming lovely girl in the world'. Hina Shamim was killed after she was knocked down as she walked a short distance from home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The pair were caught on camera at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was reportedly angry with the girl because she had allegedly been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen wearing a black top, and the victim is seen wearing white.

The chief executive of Stoke, Tony Scholes, is hopeful they can keep their goalkeeper, Asmir Begovic, who is entering the final year of his contract. Although Begovic has been linked with other clubs during his time at the Britannia Stadium, Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old's ambitions. 'Clearly Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and we are very keen to keep him at the club,' he told The Sentinel. 'I think when you've got extremely good players it is only natural that there will be speculation about their future.'

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger sent the video to his boss at Ritchies Coachlines. In the video, the driver can be seen flipping through pages while the bus is moving. When the bus stopped at traffic lights, he moved his head to look at the paper. His boss, Andrew Ritchie, was embarrassed by the driver's actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play against Leicester City on Saturday. Reid hurt his hamstring in a game with Chelsea on March 4, but he is back to full training now. Enner Valencia will not play. He missed the last two games because of a toe injury at home in mid-Mrracle, but Allardyce says he is not match fit. West Ham centre back Winston Reid (right) tussles with Tottenham's Mousa Dembele in February .

Five days before their wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway. Brittany died, and John was badly hurt. Doctines told he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, stuck in a wheelchair. But against all the odds, John recovered. On March 24, the 25-year-old assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College helped lead his team to a championship.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to his best form after recovering from injury. The Brazil international played 16 games in 19 matches from late November, which helped the team win. Until a problem in February's Merseyside derby, he missed 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Sick of awkward father-daughter photos? A Japanese photographer named Yûki Aoyama has found a funny way to make them better. In her pictures, the daughter smiles at the camera while her father leps into the air. The photos are from her new book called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old who is suspected of robbing a bank in broad daylight and running off with £3,000 in cash. The robbery happened at 12.30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is about 5ft 9in to 6ft and was wearing black clothing. The white male suspect, who has greying black hair and wore glasses, was captured on camera inside the bank. Detectives said no one was injured during the robbery and they were 'confident' the public would be able to identify the suspect.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has lifted Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. The ban, which was originally imposed by the Confederation of African Football, kept Morocco out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments.

Morocco was also fined $1 million by the CAF. The organization also demanded an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco pulled out of the tournament due to fears related to the Ebola epidemic.

Morocco had previously pulled out as hosts of the African Cup of Nations, which was eventually won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. The country can now compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd says Jason Denayer’s successful loan at Celtic means he is ready to play for Manchester City next season. This would likely stop Celtic from keeping the Belgian defender for another year. However, Boyd believes this move will encourage other young players to join Celtic. Denayer, 19, has also played for Belgium recently.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing people who doubted him. This great season for the 23-year-old player has had ups and downs since he first became a star on the international stage. England manager Roy Hodgson has kept believing in Townsend, who paid back that trust with an amazing goal at Juventus Stadium. Andros Townsend scored England's equaliser in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. Townsend celebrates his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason (left) and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The deal was finalized at a meeting on Tuesday, where the legal team representing Wanda Madrid Investment signed off on buying 726,707 shares for €45 million (about £32.8 million). The purchase was first announced in January, but needed two meetings to be officially completed. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin hopes to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the trip brought "very fond memories," despite reports that he received death threats in the days before the friendly.

Conce took over Italy in August after the team failed to advance from the World Cup group stage last summer. His first seven months in charge have been unstable. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to draw 2-2 with Bulgaria last Saturday. Reports say Conte received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibs can catch Rangers for second place. His team, Dumbarton, have played both Rangers and Hibs already this season and will play them again at the end. But while Rangers are doing well now - they beat Hibs and Cowdenbeath while Raith beat Hibs - Murray thinks the power will swing back to Hibs before long. He believes Rangers will struggle to keep up their pace.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in World Cup qualifiers. Even though he was in the match squad, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. Mignolet shared photos of him posing in a pilot's cockpit on Facebook.

A large rural estate is for sale for £6 million. The property, called Chyknell Hall Estate, is near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It has 200 acres of land, a Grade II-listed manor house, five cottages, a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green.

The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms. It was built in 1814 and has only had two owners. Experts think it will attract A-list buyers because the secluded grounds offer complete privacy.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one, who was then arrested. The incident happened at El Centro College. A student named Charles Adams recorded the incident on his phone last Wednesday. He saw the officers approach the students while they were waiting for a bus outside the downtown campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke their permanent manager. The 39-year-old, who took the job temporarily in February, has only lost once in seven games. He signed a three-year deal after chairman Jim Mann shook his hand.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football calendar takes place. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to keep dominating at home this season.

However, the two big rivals meet with 31 points and nine positions separating them in the standings. Even though there is a gap, the stakes are still high whenever these two clubs meet.

Jurgen Klop (centle) celebrates with his Borussia Dortmund players after their victory against Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stuck at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her on her plane. She was crying because she was only allowed two pieces of hand luggage, but had brought two. She offered to pay to put the second bag in the hold, but was told she could only pay by credit card. She could not pay because she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with a single punch to the back of the head. The punch was so hard it made a loud cracking sound, and Mr. Potts fell down and died.

Robson had a history of violent offenses. He was drunk at his grandfather's funeral when he stepped in to break up a fight outside a sports bar. At Newcastle Crown Court, he was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the crime that happened in November last year outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Arsenal. She hit the ball into the corner after her teammates, Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood, accidentally bumped into each other other at the ball.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.'

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not realize what their mind and body actually need during these resting hours to feel refreshed every day. The Sleep Health Foundation released a study showing that 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep on a daily basis. According to Chair Professor David Hillman, those misplaced hours of sleep must be paid back to be functional for the entire week. The average adult needs around eight hours of sleep per night, with a recommended range of seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb. The argument escalated into a physical fight where a woman brandished a crowbar and shouted racist slurs at a group of men. The men fought back, and a scuffle broke out.

Everyone is watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him from Real Madrid this summer. Sportsmail writer Pete Jenson looks at the Spain under 21 defender. Why are English clubs so keen? His buy-out clause is currently set at £13.5m. When you consider that Luke Shaw – of a similar age and potential – cost £27m it would be silly not to be interested; although there would be also be reservations about his suitability to the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) in action for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He saved two teenagers after a 59-year-old man allegedly pulled a gun on them in Salem. The stranger used his helmet to knock the gun away, letting the teens run off.

Tim Sherwood wants Ron Vlaar to play well so Aston Villa can avoid being relegated. Sherwood wants to see the fit player help the team finish strongly. He reminded people that Vlaar was a good player at the World Cup in Brazil last year. Vlaar played for Holland in the semi-finals, but missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina, which led to links with Manchester United. Aston Villa will welcome back their club captain Ron Vlaar as they head to Old Trafford on Saturday. The commanding Dutch centre-back returns from injury to help Villa in their battle against relegation.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to build his own team next year if the club stay up. Randy Lerner is in talks with a possible new owner. But Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa safe first, before making changes in the summer. Christian Benteke scored as Villa thranh Sunderland last month.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, Manchester City's manager, Pep Guardiola, said his young players are not ready for the first team. This means players like Denyer might have to return to City to fill a space in the team. Denyer has done well while playing for Celtic this season on loan from Manchester City.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate date before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper for the summer. Fraser Forster hurt his knee during the 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago, and doctors say he could be out for four to twelve months. Koeman is unsure exactly when Forster will return but thinks Kelvin Davis can cover for him. However, Koeman may have to bring in a new keeper if Forster is out longer than expected.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team missed a penalty chance in a Championship loss to Birmingham. Birmingham scored first through Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire pulled a goal back for Rotherham. However, Rob Kiernan handled Matt Derbyshire clumsily near the hour mark, and Derbyshire went down in the box. Referee Dean Whitestone waved away appeals for a penalty, leaving Evans visibly enraged as Birmingham held out. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear to see. Holland’s national team has already let more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they let in the whole qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. And still, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month. The game's governing body has come under fire from Caley Thistle fans for scheduling the match for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18 - before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. Now the Parkhead club have made their feeling known after ticket prices were set at £23 for the North and South stands, with the East Stand being £15 for adults and £5 for concessions.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray says the club was forced to leave the stock market because of the previous board's mistakes. He insists the new board's future plans and investments are still in place.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday night. Nine months after they met at the World Cup, the Three Lions faced the Italians again in a friendly match at the Juventus Stadium. Hopes were high after seven straight wins, but Roy Hodgson's men struggled in the first half. They deservedly fell behind to a Graziano Pelle header in Turin. England captain Wayne Rooney gave instructions during the 1-1 draw against Italy on Tuesday night. Rooney said he and the rest of the England players were upset by their first half performance.

Two of Dundee United's fan groups are angry about the club's leadership. They are upset that 25 percent of the money made from selling four players went as as a fee to unnamed parties. They also disagree with how the chairman is supposedly investing his money. The club's board says the criticism is wrong because the team has been winning on the field.

Gary Locke will be confirmed as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. This comes exactly eight weeks after he was asked to take charge until the end of the season. The Rugby Park club will make the announcement on Friday morning. Locke, the former Hearts boss, has been given a three-year deal. On Thursday, the 39-year-old paid tribute to the players who helped him win favor with new chairman Jim Mann. He replaced Allan Johnston on a caretaker basis in February.

Chinese parents love having child prodigies. Some have 10-year-old children who started university early, and others have four-year-olds who dance like Michael Jackson. A new basketball star is becoming famous online. A viral video from China shows a small boy with amazing basketball skills that would shame many professional players. The five-year-old boy is named Mai Zizhuo. He has been shooting hoops since he was two and a half years old, reported the People's Daily Online. The video starts with the small player scoring many hoops before dribbling two basketballs while running around.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the rest of the season. The 22-year-old got a torn knee ligament while playing for Austria against Bosnia. He was out for three months earlier this season with a partial knee ligament tear. 'I am bitterly disappointed,' he said. 'But I have a big aim and that is to be there at the season finale.'

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace the injured Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract and will join the team once paperwork is completed. At 30, Tilse has made 200 appearances in Australia and will link up with his old teammate Terry Campese. He is a like-for-like replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole will play in Sunday's final, even though it comes just one week after his cousin's death.
